input: A shell-and-tube heat exchanger installed in a refinery preheat train was used to heat cooling water, and its performance was assessed in order to establish how effectively it was transferring heat under the conditions studied. The duty of the exchanger was found to be 687 kW, which represents the total rate at which heat was being transferred from the hot stream to the cold stream. The hot stream entered the exchanger at a temperature of 150 °C and left at 110 °C, so it was cooled through a temperature change of 40 K as it gave up its heat. The cold stream, the cooling water being heated, entered at a much lower temperature of 25 °C and left at 50 °C, so it was warmed through a temperature change of 25 K. Because the two streams pass through the exchanger in opposite directions, the temperature difference that drives the heat transfer varies along the length of the unit, and it is therefore characterised by the log-mean temperature difference, which in this case was 92.3 K; the terminal differences at the two ends of the exchanger, obtained from the inlet and outlet temperatures, are 100 K and 85 K respectively. The installed heat transfer area of the exchanger is 25.7 m2, and bringing the duty, the area, and the log-mean temperature difference together gives an overall heat transfer coefficient of 290 W m-2 K-1. It is important to note that fouling of the heat transfer surfaces was assessed on the basis of a single 90-day run, and no cleaning cycle has yet been completed, so the picture of fouling behaviour that is available remains limited at this stage.
target: A shell-and-tube exchanger in a refinery preheat train heats cooling water at a duty of 687 kW. The hot stream enters at 150 °C and leaves at 110 °C, a fall of 40 K. The cold stream enters at 25 °C and leaves at 50 °C, a rise of 25 K. The terminal temperature differences are 100 K at the end where the hot stream enters and 85 K at the end where it leaves, and the log-mean temperature difference computed from them is 92.3 K. The installed area is 25.7 m2. Duty divided by area and by the log-mean temperature difference gives the overall coefficient: 290 W m-2 K-1 for the exchanger as it ran. The coefficient bundles the two film resistances and the wall resistance into a single figure, and the run does not separate them. The duty is the rate at which heat passed from the hot stream to the cold stream during the run, and the streams run countercurrently, so each end of the exchanger pairs the entering stream of one side with the leaving stream of the other. The coefficient is a property of the run, not of the exchanger in any state. Fouling was assessed from a single 90-day run, and no cleaning cycle has been completed, so the surfaces during the run carried whatever deposit the run had laid down, and the coefficient is the fouled value over that period. What the coefficient becomes after cleaning, and how quickly it falls again, are not established by a single run with no cleaning in it. The reported figures therefore fix the performance in the state in which the exchanger was measured, with the fouling condition of the run behind them. The figures are also internally consistent: the duty, the area, and the temperature difference return the stated coefficient, and no figure in the set depends on a measurement outside the run.
